hints: Look closely at the four options and ask yourself, which ones belong only to DNA and which belong only to RNA? Remember a virus has one or the other, never both.
Think about the bases. Which base is shared by both DNA and RNA, while thymine is replaced by uracil in RNA?
walkthrough:
**Recall what every virus has**

All viruses have nucleic acid as their genetic material. That is either DNA or RNA, but never both in the same virus.

So we need something found in both DNA and RNA.

**Sort the sugars and bases**

Ribose is the pentose sugar in RNA only. Deoxyribose is the pentose sugar in DNA only.

Similarly, thymine is a base found in DNA only. In RNA it is replaced by uracil.

**Find the common base**

Adenine is a purine base found in both DNA and RNA. It pairs with thymine in DNA and with uracil in RNA.

Therefore adenine must be present whether the virus is a DNA virus or an RNA virus.

options.A: Ribose is only in RNA, so DNA viruses do not contain it.
options.B: Deoxyribose is only in DNA, so RNA viruses do not contain it.
options.C: Adenine is present in both DNA and RNA, so it is present in all viruses.
options.D: Thymine is only in DNA, RNA viruses use uracil instead, so it is not in all viruses.
